title: Will ex-RCMP inspector, accused of being an agent for China, testify in B.C. court?
text:
Will ex-RCMP inspector, accused of being an agent for China, testify in B.C. court?
Crown case against Bill Majcher ends early. Defence lawyer gets more time to plan next steps.
The lawyer for an ex-RCMP inspector charged with foreign interference on behalf of China said he was caught off-guard April 22 when the Crown decided not to call another witness.
“The Crown is closing its case,” prosecutor Charles Hough nonchalantly told B.C. Supreme Justice Martha Devlin in Vancouver.
Ian Donaldson, who represents Bill Majcher, asked for, and got, adjournment until April 23, so he could seek instruction from his client on next steps.
Surprise
“Wasn’t my expectation at the end of the day yesterday,” Donaldson said, indicating he was expecting another witness.
“Well, you know how litigation goes, Mr. Donaldson,” Devlin said.
“Oh, yes,” he replied.
The Crown had been expected to call Kim Marsh, a friend of Majcher and former RCMP international organized crime unit commander who is now a consultant in compliance, due diligence and anti-money laundering and advises governments on citizenship by investment.
Donaldson said he learned only within the last hour that it had become “a very different case… than I was expecting.”
Next steps
The trial was originally expected to go as long as three weeks when it was planned for judge and jury, but was streamlined when it went ahead with Devlin alone.
“I appreciate that this event this morning is perhaps not what you were expecting was going to happen, and you need to consider your position,” Devlin said to Donaldson.
She originally asked whether he could come back in the afternoon, but he said he needed more time.
“What I have to do now is I have to think about what the case is, when I’ve been expecting the case to be something different for 18 months,” he said.
Since the case shifts to the defence, Donaldson is expected to tell Devlin whether his client will testify or exercise his right to decline.
Background
Majcher pleaded not guilty April 20 to a charge under the Security of Information Act of preparing to induce by threat, accusation, menace or violence Sun Commercial Real Estate founder Hongwei “Kevin” Sun in order to convince him to return to China with his assets in May and June 2017.
The Chinese government believed he fled to Canada with $100 million.
The investigation of Majcher, led by the RCMP’s Quebec division and Integrated National Security Enforcement Team, began in September 2021 when Majcher was living in Hong Kong, where he co-founded EMIDR Ltd. (which stands for Evaluate Monitor Investigate Deter Recover). The corporate risk advisory firm is focused on asset recovery and cybersecurity and helping governments to tackle financial crime, money laundering and tax evasion.
In a pretrial ruling, Devlin said the RCMP violated Majcher’s constitutional rights with a warrantless arrest at Vancouver International Airport in July 2023.
summary: The lawyer for an ex-RCMP inspector charged with foreign interference on behalf of China said he was caught off-guard April 22 when the Crown decided not to call another witness. The Crown had been expected to call Kim Marsh, a friend of Majcher and former RCMP international organized crime unit commander who is now a consultant in compliance, due diligence and anti-money laundering and advises governments on citizenship by investment.
